content.text: Most tutorials about [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/build-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-without-stripe-honest-side-side-3|Selling Digital]]-digital-products-africa-until-you-read|build]]ing a digital store focus on the storefront. The storefront is the last thing you should configure. The backend is what makes the store work — and the backend is what most creators get wrong when they try to build without a clear sequence. In Stack 01, Google Apps Script serves as the backend Web App — it receives the NOW[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-gateways-cameroon-digital-products-step-step-deployment|COREMERCH guide to payment]]s webhook, validates the signature, confirms the transaction on-chain, logs the order to Google Sheets, and sends the delivery email via Gmail. In Stack 02, Cloudflare Workers replaces Apps Script with a faster, more scalable serverless backend that integrates natively with Supabase for order storage and Resend for email delivery. Configure the backend first, set the webhook endpoint URL in NOWPayments second, build the storefront third, and test on mainnet fourth.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The beauty of using Supabase as your order database lies in its ability to provide a scalable and secure environment for managing customer data and orders. By integrating Supabase with NOWPayments, you can create a seamless payment pipeline that allows customers to pay with over 300 cryptocurrencies, eliminating the need for traditional payment gateways like Stripe or PayPal. This infrastructure is specifically designed for digital creators who have been locked out of mainstream e-commerce platforms, providing them with a reliable and efficient way to sell their digital products online.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your Supabase-powered digital store, you'll need to set up a few key components. First, create a Supabase account and set up a new project. Next, install the necessary dependencies, including the Supabase JavaScript library and a code editor like Visual Studio Code. You'll also need to create a NOWPayments account and obtain an API key to integrate with your Supabase project. With these components in place, you'll be ready to start building your digital store.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment pipeline, you'll need to integrate NOWPayments with your Supabase project. This involves creating a new payment gateway in your Supabase dashboard and configuring the NOWPayments API to process transactions. You'll also need to set up a delivery pipeline to distribute your digital products to customers. This can be done using a service like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, which provides a secure and reliable way to store and deliver your products.
Build a sovereign commerce infrastructure without relying on Stripe or PayPal.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you're ready to go live and start processing transactions. This involves deploying your Supabase project to a hosting platform like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and configuring your NOWPayments API to process transactions. When a customer makes a purchase, the payment will be processed automatically, and the product will be delivered to their email inbox or download link. With this infrastructure in place, you can focus on creating and selling digital products, without worrying about the technical complexities of payment processing.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your digital store grows and you start to process more transactions, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to keep up with demand. This involves upgrading your Supabase plan to increase storage and bandwidth, as well as optimizing your payment pipeline to reduce latency and improve performance. You may also need to add additional features, such as analytics and reporting, to help you better understand your customers and optimize your sales funnel. With the right infrastructure in place, you can scale your digital store with confidence and reach a global audience of customers.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your Supabase-powered digital store, follow these steps: create a Supabase account and set up a new project, install the necessary dependencies, create a NOWPayments account and obtain an API key, integrate NOWPayments with your Supabase project, set up a delivery pipeline, deploy your project to a hosting platform, and configure your NOWPayments API to process transactions. With these steps complete, you'll be ready to start processing transactions and selling digital products online.
